# Sirach Chapter 3 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 3

---

**1** Listen to me, your father, O children; act accordingly, so that you may be safe.

**2** For the Lord gave the father authority over his children, and established the right of the mother over her sons.

**3** Whoever honors his father atones for sins,

**4** and whoever glorifies his mother is like one who lays up treasure.

**5** Whoever honors his father will be gladdened by his own children, and when he prays he will be heard.

**6** Whoever glorifies his father will have long life, and whoever obeys the Lord brings comfort to his mother.

**7** He who fears the Lord honors his father, and serves his parents as his masters.

**8** Honor your father in word and deed, so that his blessing may come upon you.

**9** For a father's blessing builds up the children's homes, but a mother's curse tears out their foundations.

**10** Do not seek honor for yourself by dishonoring your father; for your father's dishonor brings no honor to you.

**11** A man's honor comes from his father's glory, and a shameful mother is a reproach to her children.

**12** My child, care for your father in his old age, and do not grieve him as long as he lives.

**13** Even if his mind fails, show patience with him; do not despise him all the days of his life.

**14** For kindness to a father will not be forgotten; it will stand as an offering against your sins.

**15** In the day of your trouble it will be remembered in your favor; like frost in fair weather, your sins will melt away.

**16** Whoever abandons his father is like a blasphemer, and whoever angers his mother is cursed by the Lord.

**17** My child, go about your work with humility, and you will be loved more than a giver of gifts.

**18** The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself; and you will find favor before the Lord.

**19** Many are great and renowned, but to the humble he reveals his secrets.

**20** For great is the power of the Lord, and he is glorified by the humble.

**21** Do not seek what is too hard for you; do not investigate what is beyond your strength.

**22** Meditate on what has been given to you; you have no need of what is hidden.

**23** Do not busy yourself with what is beyond your task; for more has been shown to you than you can fully grasp.

**24** For many have been led astray by their own presumption, and false imagination has warped their thinking.

**25** Without eyes there is no light; without knowledge, no wisdom.

**26** A stubborn heart will come to grief in the end; the one who loves danger will perish by it.

**27** A stubborn heart will be burdened with troubles; the sinner piles up sin upon sin.

**28** For the proud there is no cure for their affliction; an evil plant has taken root in them.

**29** An intelligent mind will ponder a proverb; a discerning ear is the desire of the wise.

**30** Water extinguishes a blazing fire; so almsgiving atones for sin.

**31** Whoever repays a kindness is mindful of the future; when he stumbles, he will find a support.

---

## Council Notes

**On v.18 — "the greater you are, the more you must humble yourself":** This is the signature line of the chapter. All agents rendered it similarly. SOPHIA preserves it with maximal clarity. The Hebrew (Cairo Genizah MS A) reads: gadol — "the great one." The Greek kai en megalōsynē sou tapeinōs has the same force.

**On vv.3-6 and atonement through honoring parents:** Ben Sira makes a remarkable claim — honoring parents has atoning power. PNEUMA appropriately highlights this in v.3. SOPHIA makes the causal connection explicit.

**On v.19 textual note:** Absent from Vaticanus proper but present in Sinaiticus and other witnesses. EMET's note is valid; SOPHIA includes the verse.

**On v.30 almsgiving:** Greek eleēmosynē = acts of mercy/almsgiving. This anticipates the fuller treatment in ch.4. Connects the chapter's ethics: honor parents (vv.1-16), cultivate humility (vv.17-28), practice generosity (vv.29-31).
